detailed_description:
Photoreal cinematic live-action, 1881 London, 35 mm film grain, natural weight and pace.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:05. The shot begins from <Picture 2>: a wide of the great alkali plain from the northern slope: the flat grey-white salt plain running unbroken to a chain of snow-flecked peaks on the horizon, a rutted waggon track winding away across it, scattered white bones bleaching beside the ruts, under a steel-blue sky burned pale at the horizon. The camera is on the bare rock of the northern slope, level with a standing man's eye and four long strides above the plain, a 35mm lens. The white afternoon sun stands high and a little behind the camera. At the first frame The steel-blue sky fills the TOP third of frame with snow-flecked peaks along its lower edge at the height of a thumbnail. The camera pulls back off the plain across the whole shot, travelling two long strides as the heat shimmer rises off the salt in the middle distance at a normal walking pace, from 00:00 to 00:02. At 00:02 a thin skein of white dust lifts along the track where the wind takes it, and the lift continues to the last frame of the shot.
